learning_outcomes.text: Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong study for adequate professional development
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools in their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Mastery of the state of stress and deformation at a point of an elastic solid and the relationship between them
Ability to identify the different ways in which resistant elements work
Mastery of the concepts and objectives of elasticity and strength of materials
Ability to identify the types of forces, stresses and deformations
Ability to define the geometry and dimension resistant elements
Ability to calculate forces, stresses and deformations

syllabus_topics: STRESS STATE AT A POINT OF AN ELASTIC SOLID
Concept of stress. Components of the stress vector
Stress in any orientation known the principal stresses
Stress in any orientation known the principal stresses (in ETP)
Deformations around a point of an elastic solid
Unit longitudinal and unit transverse deformation
Experimental relationship between stress and strain: stress-strain diagram
Hooke's Law. Longitudinal modulus of elasticity. Poisson's ratio
Angular distortion due to shear stresses. Shear modulus of elasticity
Lamé's equations. Relationship between E, G and n
PARTICULAR CASES OF ELEMENTS SUBJECTED TO AXIAL FORCE.
Stresses in pipes and spherical tanks. Rotating rings
CALCULATION AND DESIGN OF ELEMENTS SUBJECTED TO SHEAR FORCE
Distribution of shear stresses in sections subjected to simple bending: Colignon's Theorem
Distribution of shear stresses in open thin-walled sections.
Calculation of riveted and bolted joints.
CALCULATION AND DESIGN OF CONTINUOUS AND VARIABLE SECTION BEAMS SUBJECTED TO BENDING
Concept of solid of equal bending strength
Calculation of beams with cover plates
Bending moment and shear force diagrams
CALCULATION AND DESIGN OF ELEMENTS SUBJECTED TO ASYMMETRICAL AND COMPOUND BENDING
Asymmetrical bending: Distribution of normal stresses
Asymmetrical bending: Neutral axis of a section
Compound bending: Distribution of normal stresses
Compound bending: Neutral axis of a section
Concept and calculation of central core
Combined bending and torsion. Strength criterion.
Application of Elasticity Theory to stress calculation
assessment_rules: A minimum weighted score of 5 out of 10 is required to pass the course, except if a student scores maximum on the global exam, resulting in a 10 for the total course. Laboratory practices account for 10% of the final grade, requiring a report and experimental work, with the grade retained for subsequent years. For progressive evaluation, each partial control must be 5 or higher, and practices passed; the final grade is 10% from practices and 90% from the average of partials. The global test requires a minimum of 4 on the exam and a total of 5, comprising 30% from progressive controls, 60% from the global test, and 10% from practices; the extraordinary call uses 90% for the final exam (minimum 5) and 10% for practices.
